text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Nafta Polska SA holding will not produce information documents for prospective investors until next month, due to a delay caused by the CPN distribution chain's restructuring, the holding's president Marek Foltynowicz said.

- The Plock-based Bizon tractor maker has formed the Ukraina SP joint venture with the Kowel-based Kowelfirmaz plant to assemble Rekord tractors in Ukraine. Bizon holds 51 percent, Kowelfirmaz 47 percent and Ukraine's agriculture ministry two percent in the new firm, Bizon board member Pawel Tomaszewski said.

- The Dutch-based Eurobalance fund will acquire a 21 percent stake in the Alpex Karlino chipboard maker worth $4.5 million. The proceeds will finance modernisation and development of Alpex's chipboard production facilities, the plant's president Jacek Czayka said.

- The planned service charge increases by state-owned telecom monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) and the Post Office are unjustified, Poland's Consumer and Competition Protection Office (UOKK) said. The UOKK will institute legal proceedings against the two firms.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's demand for car credits rose in January despite the central bank's warnings about possible interest rate rises, Invest Bank and Polish Investment Bank (PBI) said.
- The Lodz province governor demanded liquidation of the Dywilan carpet maker and transfer of its assets to a joint stock company controlled by Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy (PBG) bank.

- Slupsk province, northern Poland, reported the country's record unemployment rate of 27.5 percent, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. The lowest unemployment, 6.9 percent, was reported in Warsaw, GUS said.
- Around 60 textile manufacturers will exhibit at the two-day Gallux-Show fair to start on January 23 in Bialystok, organisers said.
- The city of Leszno plans to issue munibonds in the fourth quarter of 1997 once the project's feasibility has been approved by Bank Zachodni.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Investments on international capital markets will present a competitive alternative to hard currency deposits in Polish banks, Pioneer PDM brokerage house president Jacek Adamski said.
ZYCIE
- The Bydgoszcz-based BFK cable maker's net profit in 1996 was 24.4 million zlotys. This year it will reach 31.5 million zlotys, the company forecast said.
- Philips now holds a 72 percent stake in the Pabianice-based Polam electric bulb maker. The concern plans to invest $30 million in Polam's development by 2000.
PARKIET
- Companies from OECD countries will be allowed to trade their stock on the Warsaw bourse following permission by the Polish Securities Commission (KPW).
- The Katowice-based Energomontaz-Poludnie electic machinery maker and construction firm will apply for a listing on the Warsaw bourse in mid-1997, the company said.
